text:
Anaheim won this game on special teams and lost the rest of it. All three Ducks goals came on the power play, and Mikael Granlund's tip-in at 4:14 of overtime ended it after Cutter Gauthier and Leo Carlsson set it up. Florida went 0 for 4 with the man advantage and outplayed Anaheim in nearly every other way: 72 shot attempts to 42, and 2.62 to 1.05 in expected goals at even strength. By the quality of chances, the Panthers deserved to win 69 percent of the time.

Gauthier was the difference, scoring twice on the power play (a snap shot at 16:18 of the first and another 47 seconds into the second) and adding an assist on the winner. Florida answered the first one in 51 seconds, when Carter Verhaeghe tipped one in, and Brad Marchand tied it at 2 with 1:50 left in regulation. Anaheim's lead never felt secure, and Florida's pressure was steady in the first two periods and strongest in the third, when the Panthers held the Ducks to 0.17 expected goals.

Lukas Dostal made the difference in the crease. Florida's chances were worth 3.76 expected goals, and he allowed two, finishing 1.76 goals above expected. Jacob Markstrom, behind a team that blocked 20 shots, gave up three on 2.59 expected. Anaheim took the extra point by converting its chances when penalties handed them over, and Florida left with one point and a game it controlled.
